description: This medieval fortress in Northumberland stood in for the grounds of Hogwarts in the first two films. Its Outer Bailey is where young wizards took their very first broomstick flying lesson.
funFact: The castle now runs real broomstick training sessions for visitors on the same lawn used in the films.

description: A sweeping 21-arch railway viaduct in the Scottish Highlands, crossed by the steam train carrying students north to school. The curve above Loch Shiel is one of the most recognisable rail views in the world.
funFact: A real steam service, the Jacobite, still crosses the viaduct in summer, and crowds gather on the hillside to watch it pass.

description: Rolling sheep farmland near Matamata became the Shire, complete with round green doors set into the hillsides. The set was rebuilt in permanent materials for the later Hobbit trilogy and is now open to visitors.
funFact: The oak tree above Bag End is artificial: its thousands of leaves were individually attached by hand.

description: A private nature reserve on Oʻahu's windward coast where steep, jungle-covered ridges plunge into wide grassy valleys. Its dramatic scenery has doubled for a prehistoric island in several blockbuster productions.
funFact: Ka'a'awa Valley at the ranch has hosted so many productions that tours point out film sites from more than 50 movies and shows.

description: Thousands of sandstone pillars rise through the mist in this Hunan forest park. Their otherworldly shapes are widely cited as an inspiration for the floating mountains of an alien moon.
funFact: After the film's release, one of the park's pillars was renamed the 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain'.

description: A two-level steel bridge over the Seine, with a metro viaduct running above a colonnaded walkway. Its repeating iron arches create a natural hall-of-mirrors effect that suits a story about dreams within dreams.
funFact: The bridge offers one of the best close-up views of the Eiffel Tower, only a few hundred metres away.

description: A vast wilderness of frozen rivers, pine forest and Rocky Mountain peaks west of Calgary. The production chased natural light and real snow here to capture a brutal frontier survival story.
funFact: Much of the film was shot using only natural light, often limiting the crew to a short window of filming each day.

description: A jagged rock island 12 km off the Kerry coast, crowned by the beehive huts of a 6th-century monastery. Its stone stairways made a fitting hideaway for a legendary hermit at the edge of the galaxy.
funFact: Skellig Michael is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to thousands of puffins each summer.

description: Matmata's traditional Berber homes are dug into the ground around circular courtyards. One of them, now a hotel, became a desert farmer's homestead on a twin-sunned planet.
funFact: You can still stay overnight in the hotel and eat in the courtyard dining room seen on screen.

movie: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
description: A temple façade carved straight into rose-red sandstone, reached through a narrow canyon called the Siq. On screen its entrance hid the resting place of a legendary relic.
funFact: The Treasury is around 2,000 years old and was carved by the Nabataeans from the top down.

description: A protected desert valley of red sand and towering granite and sandstone mountains in southern Jordan. Its scale and silence made it the backdrop for one of cinema's grandest desert epics.
funFact: Wadi Rum's Mars-like landscape has since stood in for the Red Planet in several science-fiction films.

description: Baroque gardens of fountains, hedges and statues with the fortress on the hill behind. Children danced around the Pegasus fountain and up the garden steps in a famous singing montage.
funFact: Salzburg still runs daily themed tours that visit the gardens, the gazebo and the lakeside villa used in the film.

description: Rome's largest Baroque fountain, where Neptune rides a shell chariot across a wall of travertine. A runaway princess paused here for a haircut on her day of freedom in the city.
funFact: Visitors toss in an estimated €1.5 million in coins each year, which is collected and donated to charity.

description: A pine-covered island in the Sporades with whitewashed harbour towns and hidden coves. A tiny chapel perched on a rock above the sea hosted the film's joyful wedding scene.
funFact: Reaching the clifftop chapel of Agios Ioannis means climbing more than 100 steps carved into the rock.

description: A glacier-carved valley of brooding peaks and moorland in the western Highlands. A classic car pulled over on the road through the glen as a secret agent headed home to his roots.
funFact: The pyramid-shaped mountain Buachaille Etive Mòr at the head of the glen is one of the most photographed peaks in Scotland.

description: A sheltered cove of white sand and turquoise water enclosed by limestone cliffs. It played the secret paradise beach that travellers risk everything to find.
funFact: The bay was closed for several years to let coral and wildlife recover from mass tourism, and reopened with strict visitor limits.

description: A hotel occupying the top floors of a Shinjuku skyscraper, with a jazz bar overlooking the endless city lights. Two sleepless strangers drift through its quiet corridors and meet at the bar.
funFact: On clear days the hotel's upper floors have views all the way to Mount Fuji.

description: The world's tallest building, a glittering 828-metre spire rising above Downtown Dubai. Its glass façade was the stage for a heart-stopping climb high above the desert city.
funFact: The lead actor performed the climb himself, secured by cables that were digitally removed afterwards.

description: A crevassed outlet glacier tumbling from Europe's largest ice cap in Vatnajökull National Park. Its blue-grey ice became a frozen world explored by astronauts searching for a new home.
funFact: Svínafellsjökull also appeared as a wintry land beyond a great wall in a hit fantasy TV series.

description: One of the oldest deserts on Earth, where towering dunes meet the cold Atlantic coast. Its endless orange sand hosted a relentless high-speed chase across a post-apocalyptic wasteland.
funFact: The production moved to Namibia after unexpected rain turned the original Australian desert location green with wildflowers.

description: The flagship jewellery store on the corner of Fifth Avenue and 57th Street in Midtown Manhattan. A lone figure in an evening gown gazes into its windows at dawn in one of cinema's most iconic openings.
funFact: The store opened especially early on a Sunday so the opening scene could be shot on an empty Fifth Avenue.

description: India's busiest metropolis, from crowded railway platforms to vast informal neighbourhoods. The grand Gothic station hosts the film's exuberant closing dance on its platforms.
funFact: The station is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and serves millions of commuters every single day.

description: Sandstone buttes rise from the red desert on the Navajo Nation along the Arizona–Utah border. A long-distance runner finally stopped on the highway here after years of crossing the country.
funFact: The stretch of US-163 where he stops is now marked informally as 'Forrest Gump Point' and draws photographers daily.

description: A walled medieval city of limestone streets and terracotta roofs on the Adriatic coast. Its old town was transformed into a glamorous casino city on a distant planet.
funFact: You can walk the full 2 km circuit of the city walls, which have protected Dubrovnik since the Middle Ages.
